intro.text: Fifth Third Bancorp (the “Bancorp” or “Fifth Third”), an Ohio corporation organized in 1975, is a bank holding company (“BHC”) as defined by the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the “BHCA”), and has elected to be treated as a financial holding company (“FHC”) under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act of 1999 (“GLBA”) and regulations of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the “FRB”). The Bancorp is a diversified financial services company headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio and is the indirect holding company of Fifth Third Bank, National Association (the “Bank”). As of December 31, 2025, Fifth Third had $214 billion in assets and operates 1,130 full-service Banking Centers and 2,199 Fifth Third branded ATMs in Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana, Michigan, Illinois, Florida, Tennessee, West Virginia, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina and Alabama.

x.name: Comerica Incorporated
f: Business Combination Recognized Asset Acquired, Other Short Term Investments
Business Combination, Recognized Asset Acquired, Debt Securities, Available for Sale

s.t: Excluding the initial impact of the Comerica acquisition, the increase in average interest-earning assets reflected an increase in average commercial loans and leases of $4.3 billion and an increase in average taxable securities of $2.7 billion, partially offset by a decrease in average other short-term investments of $4.7 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in the prior year.

The increase in total investment securities reflects the impact of the Comerica acquisition, including $7.2 billion of available-for-sale debt and other securities, $3.7 billion of held-to-maturity securities, $170 million of trading debt securities and $141 million of equity securities acquired on February 1, 2026.

The decrease was primarily driven by the strategic redeployment of liquidity into investment securities to proactively manage interest rate risk, wholesale funding maturities that were not replaced, as well as growth in loans and leases during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, partially offset by an increase in core deposits, including the migration of former off-balance-sheet Comerica investment sweep balances onto the balance sheet during the third quarter of 2026, and other short-term investment balances acquired in connection with the acquisition of Comerica.

Under the terms of the merger agreement, each outstanding share of Comerica’s common stock was converted into the right to receive 1.8663 shares of Fifth Third Bancorp common stock and each outstanding share of Comerica’s preferred stock was converted into the right to receive one share of a newly created series of preferred stock with comparable terms issued by the Bancorp.

On February 1, 2026, the Bancorp issued 16,000,000 depositary shares, representing 400,000 shares of 6.875% fixed-rate reset non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock, Series M to the holders of Comerica’s 6.875% fixed-rate reset non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock, Series B that were outstanding on January 30, 2026.

These benefits were partially offset by increases in interest expense primarily due to higher average balances of interest-bearing core deposits and long-term debt primarily driven by the Comerica acquisition as well as lower yields on average loans and leases and average other short-term investments resulting from lower short-term market rates.

On an average basis, interest-earning assets increased $76.5 billion, or 40%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in the prior year primarily driven by the initial impact of the Comerica acquisition on February 1, 2026 which included the acquisition of $46.5 billion of commercial loans and leases, $4.1 billion of consumer loans, $11.3 billion of other short-term investments and $11.2 billion of securities.

The increase in average interest-bearing core deposits was primarily due to the migration of former off-balance-sheet Comerica investment sweep balances onto the balance sheet during the third quarter of 2026 as well as higher offering rates from promotional offers and branch expansion leading to growth in the number of average consumer customer accounts as well as higher average balances per consumer customer account.

The decrease in the effective tax rate for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in the prior year is primarily due to an increase in tax credits and other tax benefits from CDC investments, net of proportional amortization, partially offset by higher nondeductible expenses related to the Comerica acquisition that would not be expected to affect the effective tax rate in future years.

Interest checking deposits increased $7.0 billion, or 11%, from December 31, 2025 primarily due to the migration of former off-balance-sheet Comerica investment sweep balances onto the balance sheet during the third quarter of 2026 as well as certain Comerica legacy deposit products that were simplified into more modern interest checking products resulting in a shift from money market deposits into commercial interest checking deposits during the third quarter of 2026.

The changes in the estimated EVE sensitivity profile from December 31, 2025 were primarily related to changes in forward interest rate expectations and an increase in interest-bearing and noninterest-bearing deposits reflecting the impact of the Comerica acquisition, partially offset by growth in the investment securities and cash flow hedge portfolios.

Additionally, on February 1, 2026, the Bancorp issued 16,000,000 depositary shares, representing 400,000 shares of 6.875% fixed-rate reset non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock, Series M to the holders of Comerica’s 6.875% fixed-rate reset non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock, Series B that were outstanding on January 30, 2026.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
